messages:
Maya (Eng-ML): bringing up lark-embed-lite v0 (channel-wise int4) on staging. initial quick checks show recall@1 drop for short queries, ~8% absolute vs fp16. anyone seen this pattern on compact models?
Drew: saw similar with other compact/distilled models when using symmetric per-channel int4. could be quantizing low-variance dims too aggressively. what was your quant scheme?
Maya (Eng-ML): per-channel symmetric, clip at 99.5th percentile. ran 10k short-query holdout (short = <16 tokens). details below.
CI-Bot: eval job #4823 finished -> s3://redwood-artifacts/evals/4823/results.json
Sophia: here's the quick paste from the job: 
``
holdout: 10k short-queries
model: lark-embed-lite-v0
fp16 recall@1/5/10: 0.71 / 0.86 / 0.91
int4 (per-channel) recall@1/5/10: 0.63 / 0.82 / 0.89
silhouette: fp16 0.34  int4 0.27
avg cosine shift (query->positive): -0.04
```
Eli: ouch. that's a meaningful R@1 regression. silhouette drop suggests cluster structure harmed, not just a uniform scaling. did you check per-dim sign flips / saturation?
Maya (Eng-ML): quick dim stats show a handful of dims with kurtosis spike pre-quant. attaching UMAP snapshot: https://img.redwood.internal/umap/lark-int4-short-2026-03-18.png
Kai: possible fixes to try: asymmetric per-channel, per-channel zero-point, or small bias folding. also try post-quant local rescale (PCA on top-k dims).
Drew: experimental plan: 1) run asymmetric per-channel int4 2) run per-tensor int4 for comparison 3) compute per-dim variance ratio fp16/int4 and threshold dims to stay fp16 (mixed quant)
Drew: command to run diag diff:
``
python tools/compare_embed_stats.py --model lark-embed-lite-v0 --fp16 stats_fp16.json --int4 stats_int4.json --out diag.csv
```
Sophia: kicking off jobs 4827 (asymmetric pcq) and 4828 (per-tensor int4).
CI-Bot: job 4827 queued by Sophia (eval cluster).
Maya (Eng-ML): adding this to a ticket with short vs long query splits, hypothesis list, and links. @Drew @Sophia please add any extra diagnostics (knn stability, centroid drift per-class). we'll triage tomorrow.
Drew: ack. will add knn-stability scripts and per-class recall tables.
Eli: also try a tiny fine-tune on the embed head with int4 simulated noise; sometimes that recovers R@1.
Maya (Eng-ML): good idea. adding to plan. thanks all :thumbsup:
